UPSTREAM: drm/atomic-helpers: Properly avoid full modeset dance Legacy setCrtc has a nice fastpath for just updating the frontbuffer when the output routing doesn't change. Which I of course tried to keep working, except that I fumbled the job: The helpers correctly compute ->mode_changed, CRTC updates get correctly skipped but connector functions are called unconditionally. Fix this. v2: For the disable sided connector->state->crtc might be NULL. Instead look at the old_connector_state->crtc, but still use the new crtc state for that old crtc. Reported by Thierry. Fix Synaptics updater scripts output There was a typo in the Synaptics touch fw updater script that resulted in the logs not having the product ID of the touch device reported. The script seemed to work correctly, and this was just an issue with the logs that it was generating not having all of the intended info. This CL fixes that bug, so now the logs contain the product ID in question. BUG=chromium:580667 TEST=manually deployed on a Heli w/ Synaptics touchpad. After applying this patch and rebooting the logs started displaying the product ID of the touchpad. mec1322: hibernate: Don't reconfigure all GPIOs Configuring all GPIOs to INPUT / PULL_UP in hibernate is not a good idea: - INPUT / PULL_UP is not necessarially the lowest-power state (for example, if there is an onboard pull-down). - Most GPIOs should already be in lowest-power state when we're in S5. - For the few GPIOs that need to be in a different state for hibernate, we can use a board-level callback. In addition, remove mec1322 code related to restoring from hibernate state, since we always reset coming out of hibernate.
